target: test whether a growing separator of width w can always be compressed to o(2^w) exact context-independent semantic states

model.state_contract: Two boundary assignments may share one DP state only if every admissible future continuation over B gives the same SAT/UNSAT behavior for both assignments.

theorem.statement: For every w>=1, all 2^w assignments to B are pairwise distinguishable under exact arbitrary-continuation semantics. For any distinct assignments a,b choose xi on which they differ. The one-literal continuation requiring xi=a(xi) is compatible with a and incompatible with b. Therefore no exact context-independent quotient valid against every continuation can identify a and b.
theorem.consequence: A generic exact separator DP cannot defeat the 2^w frontier merely by quotienting boundary assignments under continuation-independent semantics.
theorem.scope_firewall: This does not rule out polynomial compression for special structured continuations, algebraic representations, symmetry classes, bounded-rank signatures, proof-carrying transforms, or a different global algorithm.

interpretation: R44H showed connectedness alone is not an obstruction when separator width is constant.
R44I shows that once width grows, a universal context-free semantic quotient has an exponential worst-case state space.
Therefore the next route must discover additional structure in the continuation or change representation; it cannot rely on a universal assignment quotient alone.
